title: Trash
whyItMatters: Deleted files sit in the Trash until it is emptied. A handover can pass on documents the owner thought they had removed.
source: Apple macOS User Guide, delete files (items move to the Trash); per-user Trash is the ~/.Trash folder (Unconfirmed: no Apple page names the path)
notes: TCC-protected: without Full Disk Access a live scan gets a permission skip. Items are counted by metadata; per-volume .Trashes folders are out of scope.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy anything in the Trash you still need to an external drive before emptying it.
steps: Open the Trash from the Dock and put back anything you want to keep.
Choose Finder > Empty Trash and confirm the warning.
Check that the Trash folder named in the plan is empty afterwards.
cleanup.risk: Everything in the Trash is deleted permanently and cannot be recovered after it is emptied.
cleanup.source: Apple Support, Delete files and folders on Mac: https://support.apple.com/guide/mac-help/delete-files-and-folders-on-mac-mchlp1093/mac
